chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

We came to the door of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام while we were seeking permission to enter upon him. We heard him speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then he wept, and we wept because of his weeping. Then the servant came out to us and gave us permission, so we entered upon him.

So I said: 'May Allah keep you well, we came to you seeking permission to enter upon you, and we heard you speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then you wept, so we wept because of your weeping.' He عليه السلام said: 'Yes. I remembered Ilyas the Prophet, and he was among the devoted worshippers from the prophets of the Children of Israel.'

So I said: 'Like what he used to say in his sajdah?' Then he spoke it in Syriac, and by Allah, we had not seen any priest or catholicos more eloquent in pronunciation than he was in it. Then he explained it to us in Arabic and said: 'He used to say in his sajdah: Will You punish me while I have made my hot middays thirsty for You? Will You punish me while I have rubbed my face in the dust for You? Will You punish me while I have avoided acts of disobedience for You? Will You punish me while I have kept my night awake for You?'

He عليه السلام said: 'Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. He said: Then he said: If You say, "I will not punish you," then were You to punish me, what would that be? Am I not Your servant and You my Lord? He عليه السلام said: Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. Indeed, when I promise a promise, I fulfill it.'

key_terms.أَوْحَى اللَّهُ: Allah revealed; indicating divine communication to the prophet
key_terms.إِلْيَاسَ النَّبِيَّ: Ilyas the Prophet; the prophet whose supplication is being recalled
key_terms.الْمَعَاصِيَ: acts of disobedience; sins that the supplicant says he avoided for Allah
key_terms.بِالسُّرْيَانِيَّةِ: in Syriac; the language in which the Imam عليه السلام was heard speaking
key_terms.سُجُودِهِ: his sajdah; the state of prostration in which the supplication was said
key_terms.مُعَذِّبِي: punishing me; central term repeated in the supplication
key_terms.وَعْدًا: a promise; referring to Allah’s promise not to punish him
key_terms.وَفَيْتُ بِهِ: I fulfill it; affirming that Allah fulfills His promise

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that the Imam عليه السلام knew the languages of earlier revelation and the supplication of Ilyas عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام spoke in Syriac while recalling the supplication of Ilyas عليه السلام in sajdah, demonstrating knowledge of revealed languages. It preserves a devotional supplication centered on humility, worship, and hope in Allah’s fulfilled promise. The report also reflects the Imams’ connection to the legacy of earlier prophets and scriptures.
